title: "Take the last character of the name" for an avatar initial can return a bare accent mark
assumption: The last character of a person's name is always a letter you can use as an initial.

input.display: "Jose\u0301" (decomposed \u00e9: "e" + COMBINING ACUTE ACCENT, 5 code points) and name[-1] / name.slice(-1)
input.description: Generating a one-letter avatar/initial from a user's display name by taking its first or last character, where the name arrived in decomposed (NFD) form from a different system or keyboard.

what_goes_wrong: name[-1] (Python) and name.slice(-1) (JavaScript) both return a single COMBINING ACUTE ACCENT by itself — not the letter "e" or the letter "\u00e9" a person would expect — because in a decomposed string the accent is its own trailing code point. The result is not even classified as a letter.
why: Unicode represents an accented letter either as one precomposed code point (U+00E9) or as a base letter followed by a separate combining mark (U+0065 U+0301). A combining mark always comes AFTER the base character it modifies, so taking the last code point (Python) or code unit (JavaScript) of a decomposed string can return the mark alone. That isolated mark has General Category Mn ("Mark, nonspacing"), not a letter category, which is why isalpha() and \p{L} both reject it. Shown on its own it has no base to attach to; depending on the renderer it appears floating over nothing, over a dotted-circle placeholder, or attached to whatever text precedes it.

repros.code:
import unicodedata
name = "Jose\u0301"
initial = name[-1]
print(name, len(name))
print(repr(initial), initial.isalpha(), unicodedata.category(initial))

fix: Normalize to NFC before taking a single character for display (so the accent recombines into one code point with its base), or better, take the first/last grapheme cluster (Intl.Segmenter in JS) rather than the first/last code point/code unit.

sources.title: Unicode Standard Annex #15: Unicode Normalization Forms
Unicode Technical Report #44: General Category values (Mn)

test_cases.note: An avatar-initial function should not return an isolated combining mark for this (valid, real-world) decomposed name.
